name: Chilenosuchus
isnote: Its armour resembles Typothorax and it has been placed in Typothoracisinae, but many other differences leave its position within the aetosaurs uncertain (English Wikipedia).
sum: Chilenosuchus is an aetosaur known from poorly preserved remains in the El Bordo Formation of northern Chile, of uncertain age.
wsnote: The sources consulted do not give the body length.
holotype: Described by Casamiquela (1980) from the El Bordo Formation, Antofagasta Region, Chile; the catalogue number is not given in the sources consulted.
material: The original specimens, known partly from poor-quality photographs.
biology: The sources consulted describe the armour but give no direct evidence of diet or habits.
author: Casamiquela 1980

dates_note: PBDB gives Carnian-Rhaetian (Late Triassic). English Wikipedia notes that fossil plants and invertebrates suggest a Late Carboniferous or Early Permian age for the beds, which conflicts with an aetosaur.
